orders.thesis: Calm contango uptrend continuation into pre-FOMC drift; spread neutralizes rich IV (rank 90).

decisions.rationale: The tape is CALM by every dial: VIX/VIX3M in clean contango (0.91), LPPL at zero, and both underlyings 7-9% above their 200-day averages in a persistent uptrend. My causal claim is simple trend continuation: with no macro catalyst until the July 29 FOMC, the path of least resistance over the next five sessions is a slow grind higher, and this 7-DTE spread expires two days before the Fed can interfere. The important nuance is that QQQ implied vol is expensive (IV rank 90, proxy 28.5 vs realized 27.5), so naked long calls would pay a fat vol tax — a defined-risk ATM/+10 debit spread largely cancels the vega and turns this into a nearly pure bet on direction. It sits alongside my existing SPY 743/750 call spread, so I am knowingly doubling the same directional thesis, but at one contract (~$480 max loss, under the 10% per-punt cap) the combined bullish exposure is still small against the bankroll, and both positions have hard-capped downside if the calm regime breaks.

orders.thesis: Calm-regime uptrend continuation into an event-quiet week; spread structure offsets rich IV.

decisions.rationale: The causal claim: SPY is in a CALM dynamical state, trending well above its 200dma, with a normal-contango VIX term structure and no scheduled macro catalyst (FOMC is 7/29, after every listed expiry) — conditions under which short-horizon drift has historically skewed positive. The obstacle is that implied vol is elevated versus realized (SPY IV rank 71, IV ~18.8 vs RV ~15.8; QQQ is worse at rank 92), which punishes naked long premium. So I express the trend with a defined-risk debit call spread — long the 743 ATM, short 750 — into 2026-07-24, which sells back most of the inflated extrinsic value and turns the trade into a bet that SPY simply grinds sideways-to-up over 7 sessions. Risking $350 (7% of bankroll), max loss is the debit; break-even sits roughly 0.4% above spot. I avoided QQQ deliberately: at IV rank 92 even spreads there price in more movement than realized vol supports.

tracks.name: fable-economist — claude-fable-5 thesis-driven AI-economy account (the headline experiment)

theses.title: memory-supercycle
theses.thesis: AI model scaling drives HBM demand that crowds out conventional DRAM/NAND wafer capacity (roughly 3:1 wafer conversion ratio), producing a structural memory shortage that TrendForce/Gartner see persisting into H2 2027 because new fabs (e.g. Micron Idaho) don't add output until 2027+. The market still prices memory makers as commodity cyclicals (MU ~7x forward earnings), but the earnings stream is becoming contractual: Micron has 17 strategic customer agreements, some take-or-pay, HBM sold out through 2026 with purchase orders into 2027-28, and will report RPOs going forward. As the market re-rates contracted memory revenue from 'cycle peak' to 'backlog', the multiple expands even if spot prices merely plateau. Falsifiers: DRAM contract prices turning negative QoQ, hyperscaler capex cuts, Samsung/SK Hynix flooding capacity faster than expected, or SCA cancellations.

theses.title: power-bottleneck
theses.thesis: AI datacenter buildout has made electricity the binding constraint on compute: Gartner sees global datacenter power demand +27% in 2026 (104->132 GW, 290 GW by 2030) and says AI capacity is now constrained by power availability; Goldman sees US datacenter power demand roughly doubling by 2027 with reliability risk concentrated in Mid-Atlantic/Mid-Continent. Second-order twist: consumer backlash over rate increases ($30B+ in rate-hike requests, bills +40% since 2021, moratorium bills in NY/MD) creates political friction for regulated utilities, so value migrates to (a) unregulated generators selling scarce firm capacity directly to hyperscalers (VST, CEG) and (b) the equipment layer building turbines and grid hardware (GEV, ETN, PWR), whose backlogs are policy-insensitive. Falsifiers: hyperscaler capex cuts, datacenter project cancellations exceeding Goldman's ~50-60% realization haircut, gas turbine order cancellations, or regulatory structures forcing hyperscaler self-funding that bypasses these vendors.

theses.title: memory-cost-squeeze-downstream
theses.thesis: The same memory shortage that lifts MU compresses margins downstream: IDC warns the crunch will shrink 2026 PC and smartphone shipments, OEMs are announcing memory-driven price increases on PCs/consoles/GPUs, and TrendForce sees consumer buyers hitting affordability limits. Long-only account cannot short HPQ/Dell/smartphone OEMs, so this is a MONITORING thesis: it disciplines position selection (avoid consumer-hardware longs), and if the squeeze triggers a consumer-electronics demand shock it becomes the early-warning falsifier channel for the memory-supercycle thesis itself — watch for OEM order cuts feeding back into DRAM contract price rollovers.

decisions.rationale: Web search was unavailable this session, so this decision rests on the state packet and my standing journal rather than fresh reporting — I flag that openly. The tape is CALM on every dial (VIX/VIX3M contango 0.91, LPPL zero, SPY/QQQ 7-9% over their 200-day) with no macro catalyst until the 7/29 FOMC, so nothing regime-level argues for defense. Two actions follow from keeping the book honest against the journal. First, t-002 (power-bottleneck) has sat unexpressed for ten days, which is a portfolio inconsistency: if electricity is genuinely the binding constraint on AI compute, the account should own both value-capture channels the thesis names, so I open small conviction-2 positions in VST (unregulated generation selling scarce firm capacity to hyperscalers) and GEV (turbine/grid equipment whose backlog is insensitive to the rate-payer political backlash). Second, MU is marked -7.6% against my cost with none of t-001's falsifiers showing — no DRAM contract price rollover, no capex-cut news in the packet — so I add $400, treating the drawdown as the market still pricing contracted HBM revenue as commodity-cycle earnings; this brings MU near but under its per-name cap. What proves me wrong: on t-002, gas-turbine order cancellations or datacenter project attrition beyond Goldman's realization haircut; on t-001, DRAM contract prices turning negative QoQ or hyperscaler capex cuts — either would trigger a weaken and a trim next session. Combined new outlay is ~$1,900, leaving ~$7,150 cash and six free slots, sized deliberately small because I could not verify current news this cycle.

thesis_updates.thesis: The same memory shortage that lifts MU compresses margins downstream: IDC warns the crunch will shrink 2026 PC and smartphone shipments, OEMs are announcing memory-driven price increases on PCs/consoles/GPUs, and TrendForce sees consumer buyers hitting affordability limits. Long-only account cannot short HPQ/Dell/smartphone OEMs, so this is a MONITORING thesis: it disciplines position selection (avoid consumer-hardware longs), and if the squeeze triggers a consumer-electronics demand shock it becomes the early-warning falsifier channel for the memory-supercycle thesis itself — watch for OEM order cuts feeding back into DRAM contract price rollovers.
thesis_updates.rationale: Logged with no order attached. It is the causal continuation of the memory thesis and defines the tripwire I will watch: when downstream demand destruction starts showing up in contract pricing (TrendForce already sees Q3 moderation to +13-18% QoQ driven by affordability, not supply), that is the beginning of the end of thesis 1.
